explanation: Kafka grew up in a German-speaking Jewish family in Prague, then part of Austria-Hungary. He also spoke Czech fluently, but wrote The Trial and The Metamorphosis in German.

claims.text: Franz Kafka wrote his works in German.
Kafka did not write his works in Czech, Yiddish or Hungarian.
Kafka lived most of his life in Prague, which belonged to Austria-Hungary until 1918.
Kafka grew up in a German-speaking Jewish family and also spoke Czech fluently.
Kafka wrote The Trial and The Metamorphosis in German.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Kafka is described as a German-language Jewish writer from Prague. His family was German-speaking, but Kafka also spoke and wrote in Czech. One source notes that Kafka did not write in standard High German, but rather in a Praguean German heavily influenced by the Yiddish and Czech languages.

claimResults.note: Search 13: Kafka is described as a German-language Jewish writer from Prague. The summary adds that he also spoke and wrote Czech; his literary works are in German, so the key stands. Counts at Tier B.

evidence.restatement: Kafka's literary works are all in German; he knew Czech well but wrote none of his fiction in Czech, Yiddish or Hungarian.
Kafka was born in Prague in 1883 and lived there almost all his life until 1923; Bohemia belonged to Austria-Hungary until October 1918.
